items.item: Columns by status show a count in their header (such as "In progress 5"), and a work-in-progress limit is shown where one applies
items.evidence: Column header renders a count badge: `${colTickets.length}` (e.g. 'In Progress' shows 3). No WIP limit concept exists anywhere in the code — the STATUSES array (lines 144-150) has no limit field, and no column header shows a limit or an over-limit warning.

items.item: Cards show the ticket code, a title (truncated with the full text available), the priority as a text label, the assignee's name and the due date or age
items.evidence: cardHtml() renders `${t.id}` (e.g. 'ITSD-1042'), subject text with `line-clamp-2` truncation (full text viewable by opening the edit modal), a priority pill with text label e.g. 'High'/'Critical', assignee name span (`${escapeHtml(t.assignee)}`, e.g. 'Marcus Lee'), and a due-date string from dueMeta() e.g. 'Nov 7' or 'Nov 6 (today)'.

items.item: A card can be moved without dragging (a "Move to" menu or the keyboard), and a drag-and-drop move is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: Non-drag move exists via prev/next step buttons (`data-action="prev"`/`"next"` calling moveTicketStep()), but they only step one column at a time (not a full 'Move to' status menu) and are visually hidden except on `group-hover` (no `focus-within` variant), so keyboard users tabbing to them get no visible affordance. More importantly, neither the drag-and-drop drop handler (`zone.addEventListener('drop', ...)`) nor the resulting toast (`<div id="toast" class="hidden fixed ...">`, no `aria-live`/`role="status"`) announces the move to assistive technology.

items.item: Moving to a status that needs input (such as Resolved needing a resolution note) asks for it, and a move can be undone (a toast with Undo)
items.evidence: setStatus(id, statusKey) at line 423 sets `t.status = statusKey` unconditionally for every status including 'resolved' — no resolution-note prompt is shown. showToast(msg) (line 234) only sets `toastEl.textContent = msg` with no Undo button or action.

items.item: Filters for assignee and priority, a search, and a switch to a list or table view
items.evidence: Priority filter (`#priorityFilter`), assignee filter (`#assigneeFilter`), and search (`#searchInput`, placeholder 'Search tickets...') are all present, but there is no list/table view toggle anywhere in the header or page — the board only renders as Kanban columns (`#board`).

items.item: Overdue or ageing tickets are marked with a text label, not by colour alone
items.evidence: dueMeta() appends explicit text: `return { text: `${fmtDate(iso)} (overdue)`, cls: "text-red-600 font-medium" }` for overdue tickets and `(today)` for due-today tickets, in addition to the colour class — so the status is conveyed by text, not colour alone.

items.item: Columns scroll on their own with sticky headers, and a wide board scrolls sideways without the page header scrolling away
items.evidence: Each column body is `class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto scrollbar-thin ... "` inside a column capped at `max-h-[calc(100vh-230px)]`, with the header `class="... sticky top-0 z-10 ..."`. The board itself is `<div id="board" class="flex gap-4 overflow-x-auto ...">`, scrolling horizontally independent of the page, while the page header is `<header class="... sticky top-0 z-30 ...">` and stays fixed.

items.item: An empty column shows a short empty state, and loading and an error with retry are present
items.evidence:
Empty columns do show `
No tickets
` when `colTickets.length` is 0. However the board renders from a static in-memory `tickets` array with no async fetch, so there is no loading skeleton/spinner state and no error-with-retry UI anywhere in the markup or script.

items.item: Opening a card shows its details in a side panel without losing the board's position or filters
items.evidence: Clicking a card calls openEditModal(), which shows `<div id="ticketModal" class="hidden fixed inset-0 bg-black/40 z-40 flex items-center justify-center p-4">` — a centered modal dialog with a backdrop, not a side panel.

tells: card-in-card — each status column is itself a card (`bg-slate-50 rounded-xl border border-slate-200`) containing individually bordered/shadowed ticket cards (`bg-white rounded-lg border border-slate-200 shadow-sm`)
oversized-radius — stat tiles and modal use `rounded-xl` (12px), flagged directly by the audit: "radius-scale ... div#statsBar > div.bg-white.rounded-xl: actual 12px, expected ≤8px"
rainbow-status — the five status columns are each tinted a different saturated hue (sky, amber, purple, emerald, slate) via `headerBg`/`headerText`/`color` in the STATUSES array
hover-lift — ticket cards use `hover:shadow-md transition-shadow` to elevate on hover
initials-avatar-non-person — the 'Unassigned' pseudo-assignee is rendered with the same initials-avatar treatment as real people (`{ name: "Unassigned", initials: "–", color: "bg-slate-300" }`)
notes: Core Kanban mechanics (status columns, counts, filters, search, priority/due styling) are implemented solidly, but several higher-order workflow requirements are missing outright: no WIP limits, no resolution-note gate on Resolved, no undo toast, no list/table view toggle, no loading/error states, and card details open in a centered modal rather than a side panel. Drag-and-drop works visually (dragover/drop handlers with `card-drag-over` styling) but has no assistive-technology announcement.
